title: Systems Engineering and Requirements
metaDescription: Aaryan Lath's systems engineering: requirements at Siemens and Purdue Space Program, RETHi safety trade studies, and managing an AAE 418 suborbital experiment.
hero: Aaryan approaches hardware as a system of requirements, interfaces, and trade-offs: he has managed requirements and budgets for student and industry teams, run safety trade studies for a lunar habitat, and carried systems work from an internship at Siemens into a full-time role.

evidence.context: Siemens Smart Infrastructure, Summer 2025 internship in the mechanical department at the Grand Prairie office, where Aaryan worked as a Systems Engineering Intern.
evidence.whatIDid: Approached switchboard production designs as a system: engineered neutral assemblies that resolved switchboard configuration edge cases across production designs, then moved upstream into the ordering pipeline by writing Python scripts that refined a back-end algorithm to automate the bill-of-materials generation process for orders, tying the mechanical design work to the systems that feed it.
evidence.outcome: Returned with a full-time offer, which Aaryan accepted; he joins Siemens Smart Infrastructure after graduation.

evidence.context: Purdue Space Program Satellites team, where Aaryan served as Deputy Systems Director for the BoilerBus CubeSat within an organization of 10 teams.
evidence.whatIDid: Owned the requirements baseline as Deputy Systems Director, formulating, reviewing, and refining over 200 project system-level and sub-system requirements for the BoilerBus, then performed a Systems Review in Spring 2024 to check the system and subsystem requirements against the design as it matured.
evidence.outcome: Held the requirements and Systems Review work for a 3U CubeSat program worked by roughly 40 engineers.

evidence.context: RETHi (Resilient Extraterrestrial Habitat Institute) at Purdue, where the systems engineering portion of Aaryan's research addressed safety controls for a lunar habitat.
evidence.whatIDid: Performed trade studies to evaluate candidate safety controls, assessing each option against cost and against the resilience of the habitat under a disruption to the lunar habitat, so that control selection could be weighed as a cost-versus-resilience decision rather than in isolation.
evidence.outcome: The research was presented at the summer symposium at Purdue, with the poster available from the RETHi page.

evidence.context: AAE 418, an advanced experimental design course in Purdue's School of Aeronautics and Astronautics, where Aaryan served as Project Manager for a small suborbital experiment.
evidence.whatIDid: Managed the small suborbital orbital-refuelling experiment end to end as Project Manager, creating the requirements and budgets for the effort and directing a team of 7 engineers through the design of the experiment, which was intended to be launched on a New Shepard flight.
evidence.outcome: Delivered the requirements, budgets, and team coordination for the experiment design targeted at a New Shepard flight.
